verdict: OK to lend in Pune auto components — pursue tier-2/3 ICE-and-EV-agnostic suppliers and pre-owned vehicle financiers; avoid single-OEM, engine-part-concentrated, thin-margin borrowers.
title: Pune Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## Where value and cash actually sit
**Pricing power sits with whoever owns the design; pure job-work shops have none.** CRISIL notes that complex parts like diesel fuel injection systems carry real pricing power, while engine-and-related-part suppliers face higher obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11]. So when a proposal lands, check the product mix; if more than half of revenue is engine/transmission parts for one ICE platform, ask what the EV transition plan is and who funds the tooling. Margin is squeezed from the commodity side too — ASK Automotive reported record revenue but aluminium squeezing margins [5].

## What has changed now
**Demand is strong but credit is running ahead of output.** India-wide auto-parts output (NIC 29) is up 25.2% YoY and 19.2% Apr-to-date [D], while bank credit to the sector is up 27.0% YoY — a gap of 7.8 pp [D]. That gap is where over-lending hides. Maharashtra GST collections are growing 8.6% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D], so the local pull is real. Peer results confirm the volume: Motherson Sumi Wiring profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore on revenue up 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4], and Lumax beat Q2 2026 estimates and lifted its outlook [7]. Note the CNBC TV18 piece is from April 2026 and flags margin pressure from commodity risk [6] — treat it as dated context, not current.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-2/3 suppliers with two or more OEM customers, EV-agnostic tooling, and a genuine aftermarket leg.** The Pune pre-owned car market is booming — dealers report bookings up 40% since last year on affordability and easy financing [1] — so used-vehicle dealer and NBFC-partner lending is a live adjacent opportunity. MOTOTECH 2026 in Chinchwad put EV readiness and MSME collaboration centre stage [2], and the components and aftermarket show runs in Pune this November [3]; use these to source borrowers, not to justify them. Structure against receivables with a charge on current assets, keep Debt/EBITDA inside 2.5-2.75x [10], and take stock statements plus OEM payment advices every month.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days drifting past the 160-170 day band [10], a single OEM crossing half of revenue, and aluminium or steel input spikes not passed through [5].** If any of these appear, cut limits and ask for the customer's hedging policy — ICRA's methodology treats hedging policy and exposure relative to profits as a core analytical focus [8]. Pune-specific data is thin: the sources tell us about events and used-car demand, not about component-maker balance sheets in the city, so lean on first principles and the peer numbers above.
